intro: Covers the US session of Wednesday 28 October (Fed decision day). Microsoft and Alphabet reported after the US close and their results are not reflected. Delayed from the 06:30 run because the US session had not closed.
footnotes: US index closes and VIX are Yahoo Finance closing prints. Trading Economics shows S&P 500 7,745.05 (+0.28%), Dow 52,586.89 (+0.25%) and VIX 16.89; Yahoo figures used.
10-year yield is Trading Economics (5.03%); Yahoo's ^TNX shows 5.05%, so the change is approximate.
Brent, gold, AUD/USD and iron ore are Trading Economics CFD reference prices; Brent was quoted between US$113.9 and US$114.1 across pages, and the iron ore print is unchanged and may be stale.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (December 2026 contract) are at about 8,881, roughly flat (-0.03% on Investing.com, -0.01% on TradingView). Applied to the prior ASX 200 close of 8,847 (-0.03% on Wednesday), that implies an open about 3 points (-0.03%) lower, near 8,844. Treat as approximate: single contract month, sources show no timestamp.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data identified in sources checked (September CPI, 4.3% year on year, was released Wednesday).
Watch the local reaction to Microsoft and Alphabet results.
what_moved: The Fed held the funds rate at 3.75-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with two officials dissenting in favour of a hike; stocks were choppy around the decision and ended modestly higher. Chair Kevin Warsh said politics played no role. Treasury yields edged up, with the 10-year at about 5.03%, and oil rose on Middle East supply concerns. S&P 500 sector performance is not available.

news.headline: Fed holds, two dissent for a hike.
news.summary: The FOMC held rates at 3.75-4.00% by 10-2; Beth Hammack and Lisa Cook preferred a hike.

news.headline: Warsh: fewer meetings ahead.
news.summary: The Fed Chair said the central bank will reduce the number of rate-setting meetings in coming years and that politics played no role in the decision.

news.headline: Australian inflation lifts to 4.3%.
news.summary: September annual CPI rose to 4.3%, a six-month high, lifting RBA hike expectations and pushing AUD/USD above US$0.70 to a five-week high.

news.headline: Oil firmer on supply risk.
news.summary: WTI rose about 1.8% to roughly US$101.7/bbl amid reports of a Saudi refinery attack and US-Iran tensions; Brent was near US$114/bbl.

news.headline: Big Tech reports after the bell.
news.summary: Microsoft and Alphabet reported after the US close; results were not verified at publication. Microsoft had offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees.

news.headline: US 10-year yield above 5%.
news.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.03%, with the Fed on hold and inflation expectations in focus.

coming_up: Thursday 29 October (US time): US GDP and PCE price index, and the ECB rate decision. Friday 30 October: Bank of Japan decision and euro-area flash GDP.
